tldr: Crisp prices per workspace ($45-$295/mo bundling seats and AI credits); Intercom prices per seat ($29+/seat/mo) plus a separate $0.99-per-resolution AI fee — very different billing shapes for very different budgets.
Crisp is self-funded and profitable with no VC pressure behind it; Intercom is a much larger, venture-backed platform that recently renamed its parent company to Fin after its AI agent.
Both are genuinely omnichannel, but Crisp's channel list leans social/messaging (WhatsApp, Instagram, Messenger, SMS) while Intercom adds phone support that Crisp doesn't have.

Crisp's G2/Capterra scores are strong but its Trustpilot score is a rough 1.9/5 driven by billing and cancellation complaints — read the fine print before committing either budget or a long-term contract.

Pick Crisp if you want one affordable inbox for chat, WhatsApp, and social without enterprise pricing; pick Intercom if you need a more independently-proven AI agent and phone support, and can absorb per-resolution costs.

Run the actual seat math before signing anything: Crisp's $45/mo Mini plan bundles 4 seats, roughly $11/seat, while Intercom's cheapest tier is a flat $29/seat no matter how many people you add — for a small team, Crisp is doing an entire inbox for less than the cost of one single Intercom seat.

Independent hands-on review of Crisp (chatimize.com) rates it well for teams wanting AI-first, workflow-first, or hybrid support setups in one place, but flags that its AI layer is credit-metered and excluded entirely from the free plan — Intercom's Fin, by contrast, carries thousands more independent reviews behind its resolution quality, for a real price difference.

featureMatrix.toolB: Not independently tracked at comparable volume

verdict: This is really a budget-versus-scale decision more than a feature fight, and the numbers make that obvious the moment you do the per-seat math: Crisp's $45/mo Mini plan works out to roughly $11/seat for a 4-person team, while Intercom's cheapest tier is a flat $29/seat no matter how many people you add — for a small team, Crisp is doing an entire inbox, WhatsApp, and social bundle for less than the cost of one single Intercom seat. What that price gap buys Intercom is a materially more independently-proven AI agent: Fin has a large body of independent reviews behind its resolution quality, while Crisp's AI layer, well-reviewed by the hands-on practitioners who've actually used it, is still a newer, credit-metered add-on that isn't included at all on the free plan. The number that should actually worry you about Crisp isn't the AI credits, though — it's the 1.9/5 Trustpilot score, which reflects a real, specific pattern of billing and cancellation friction that G2 and Capterra's glowing reviews don't surface, because those reviewers are rating day-to-day usability, not what happens when they try to leave. My honest read: if your support volume is mostly chat and messaging, budget is tight, and you're disciplined about reading cancellation terms before you sign, start with Crisp — the math clearly favors it. If you need phone support Crisp simply doesn't have, or you want the more independently-validated AI agent and can tolerate Intercom's per-resolution costs, pay the premium for Intercom instead.
